source: real report, de-identified; see README.md. Extended from one specimen to three.
notes: Histopathology on three GI biopsy specimens. The first corpus case where finding codes are
expected to RESOLVE rather than stay null, and the first where the conditions dimension has
a true positive at all — cases 001 and 002 both expect `conditions: []`, so that set has
never scored a single item and an empty set reports as 100%.
The source document carried one specimen (ascending colon, tubular adenoma). Two more were
added — sigmoid and gastric antrum — because a single-specimen report cannot exercise site
discrimination, and because a document where SOME catalogue words are present and OTHERS are
negated is a far harder negation test than case 002, where every catalogue word was negated
uniformly. Here the model has to tell дисплазия (present, ascending colon) from дисплазия
what_this_case_exercises: positive finding_code resolution, three times over: dysplasia, polyp, inflammation — the
resolver's success path, which no case has ever run. Both case 002 codes are null.
the coded branch of the new naming rule: finding_type_text must be the catalogue's spelling
(Дисплазия / Полип / Воспаление), not the document's wording. Case 002 only exercised the
uncoded branch, where the document's own words are copied.
a three-level body site tree: colon_ascending and colon_sigmoid are both children of colon,
so the pipeline must pick the segment and not collapse to the parent. Case 002's kidney tree
is one level and only one child was in play.
severity as something other than 'unknown' for the first time: mild (низкой степени) and
moderate (умеренной степени) in the same document.
conditions with a real ICD-10 code (D12.2) — the first true positive in that dimension, and
a deliberate contrast with case 002's Z01.8, which is an encounter code and expected absent.
three negations sitting beside three positives: 'без признаков дисплазии', 'кишечная
метаплазия не выявлена', 'атрофия не выявлена' — metaplasia and atrophy are both catalogue
entries, so declining them requires reading the negation rather than declining everything.
a lab result table printed with headers and no rows, which must yield no observations
a 2020 record_date, four years before every other case, against a 2020-02-11 print timestamp
and the same 21.11.2011 statute-date distractor case 002 carries
'Количество фрагментов' — a specimen count that is not a lesion count. See judgement_calls.
a checkup list where NOTHING matches: no case has yet expected zero completions out of 22

must_not_resolve: полип @ colon_sigmoid — the sharpest negative in the corpus so far. This document FINDS a
polyp in the sigmoid, so the model has positive, matching evidence in front of it and must
still not report the existing one as resolved. Finding a thing is not resolving it. Case
002's finding negative rested on the document being silent; this one rests on the document
agreeing and the conclusion still being wrong.
эрозия @ stomach — the gastric biopsy describes inflammation and says nothing about a prior
cond-...0005 Хронический гастрит — the document actively CONFIRMS it: 'Хронический активный
гастрит умеренной степени активности'. Every previous negative in the corpus was silence or
absence of evidence; this is evidence pointing the other way. A pipeline that treats 'this
condition appears in a new document' as a state change closes it here.
The other four (B12 deficiency, iron-deficiency anaemia, NAFLD, dyslipidaemia) are plain
negatives — a GI biopsy bears on none of them.

judgement_calls: 'Количество фрагментов: 2' is expected to produce count 1, not 2. It is the number of tissue
fragments the pathologist received, not the number of adenomas. A model that copies it into
count has misread the document, and this is the case's most likely single failure. Note the
builder coerces a missing count to 1 (service.ts:178, `item.count || 1`), so 1 is also what a
correct null becomes — the expectation cannot distinguish 'said 1' from 'said nothing', only
'said 2'. That is the assertion worth having.
Хронический активный гастрит is expected as BOTH a finding (inflammation @ stomach, from the
microscopic description) and a condition (from the ЗАКЛЮЧЕНИЕ, where it is stated as a
diagnosis). A reviewer could reasonably hold that this double-counts one clinical fact. It is
scored both ways because the two dimensions mean different things — the finding is the
morphology, the condition is the diagnosis — and because a document can legitimately support
both. If this is flipped, drop the condition and keep the finding.
The tubular adenoma is expected as `dysplasia`, not `polyp`. The catalogue has no adenoma
entry; the document's own words for object 1 never say полип, and дисплазия is stated
outright. Object 2 does say полип, which is why that one is coded polyp. A reviewer who
thinks an adenoma is always a polyp would code both the same and lose the distinction the
document actually draws.
record_type is expected as 'lab', not 'procedure'. The document is issued by a laboratory
reporting on a specimen, under a lab result-table header; the endoscopy that obtained the
tissue is not described anywhere in it. Arguable — 'procedure' would be the first use of that
record_type, so if it is flipped, flip it deliberately.
'Helicobacter pylori (+)' is expected to produce NO observation. It has no numeric value, no
unit and no reference range, and no catalogue entry; it is a qualitative microbiology result
sitting inside a histology narrative. If the pipeline should carry qualitative positives, that
is a schema question, not a fixture one.
what_the_first_live_run_found: Findings 3 tp / 2 fp / 0 fn; conditions 1 tp / 3 fp / 1 fn; nothing wrongly resolved.
Held: all three findings matched on the correct site, so the sibling-segment discrimination
between colon_ascending and colon_sigmoid works. size_mm 3/3 (0,6 см -> 6). Every negation
held — no metaplasia, no atrophy, no dysplasia attributed to the sigmoid — which is the
harder version of case 002's test, since this document has positives sitting beside the
negatives. Both confirm-is-not-resolve traps held: the seeded sigmoid polyp was found again
by this document and still not closed, and Хронический гастрит was confirmed and not closed.
Zero checkups completed out of 22, and no observations invented from the empty result table.
Four defects:
1. 'Helicobacter pylori (+)' was emitted as a finding, coded null and sited to stomach. A
qualitative microbiology result became a structural finding, and because it took the stomach
slot it displaced the real gastritis finding.
2. inflammation did not resolve for 'Хронический активный гастрит' — code came back null.
The catalogue holds Воспаление and the fuzzy matcher did not bridge гастрит -> воспаление.
That is the resolver's success path failing on the third of its three chances here; the
other two (dysplasia, polyp) resolved correctly, which is itself the first time that path
has ever succeeded in this corpus.
3. severity 1/3. Both graded findings came back 'unknown' — 'низкой степени (слабая
дисплазия)' should be mild and 'умеренной степени активности' should be moderate. The first
run in which severity was scoreable at all, and it fails immediately.
4. Conditions came back as the ЗАКЛЮЧЕНИЕ sentences copied verbatim into `name` ('Тубулярная
аденома восходящей ободочной толстой кишки с дисплазией эпителия низкой степени') rather
than as diagnoses. D12.2 was picked up once, so the ICD path works, but the dimension is
largely producing prose where it should produce conditions.
Scorer limit this case exposed honestly: two findings landed on colon_ascending and two on
stomach, so findingKeyCollisions fired for the first time against a real document. The
finding-field numbers above are directionally right but not trustworthy row by row. Note that
GI documents carry no laterality, so half the site+laterality key is dead weight there and
collisions are far likelier than in the kidney case.
Operational: the first attempt timed out on extract at the 60s default and the retry took
44s. Production uses the same 60s at the same high reasoning effort, so a longer report would
fail outright. The partial-recording guard behaved correctly — classify was kept, not pruned.
